title: The Last Orchard Again
premise: Silas Underhill inherited his grandmother's failing orchard-vineyard along with crushing debts, and he has spent three years quietly selling off parcels while pretending the place still thrives. When his family reunion demands he arrive with a partner, he hires Marisol Vega, a sharp-tongued sommelier who owes him a favor, for a single fake weekend. But Marisol recognizes the rot beneath the estate's beauty and, worse, starts recognizing the man beneath his careful silence. As the harvest festival approaches, Silas must choose between selling the orchard to erase his debts and confessing both his ruin and his love; he risks everything by telling the truth at the festival, keeping the land and winning Marisol only after he stops hiding.
about_author: Theo Montrose is the pen name of a former agricultural journalist who traded crop reports for love stories set in dying rural towns. They write from a converted packing shed, convinced the best romances grow in the poorest soil.

chapters.title: Borrowed Weather
chapters.summary: Silas's POV opens with him hiding foreclosure letters in a hollow apple tree and rehearsing lies about the vineyard's health. When his sister calls to confirm he's bringing someone to the Underhill reunion, he panics and calls Marisol, the sommelier who once saved his tasting room from disaster. She agrees to one weekend, no feelings, payment in rare vintages. Emotional beat: anxious denial, the comfort of a transactional arrangement.

chapters.title: The Reunion Table
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV during the reunion weekend at the orchard farmhouse. She performs the devoted partner flawlessly, but notices the sold-off fields, the unpaid workers, the way Silas's family praises a prosperity that no longer exists. A late-night kitchen conversation cracks his armor; he admits the debts without admitting the shame behind them. His mother watches them too closely. Emotional beat: intimacy blooming inside a lie, guilt sharpening.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Marisol discovers the sale contract for the orchard hidden in his desk and confronts him: he planned to sign it the day after the festival, erasing the place where they'd grown close. A bitter quarrel erupts during festival preparations, witnessed by his family, and his sister reveals Silas once gave up a love years ago to save the farm the first time. Emotional beat: climax of loyalty versus truth, the fake romance collapsing into real heartbreak.

chapters.title: First Fruit
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, then shared. At the harvest festival, Silas publicly refuses the sale, confesses his debts to the whole town, and asks Marisol not for a favor but for a future, offering the whole orchard and the whole heart. She stays; together they plan a small honest winery from the surviving vines. Epilogue beat at the last row of trees: love in present tense at last. Emotional beat: costly honesty rewarded, quiet hope.
